evals.name: thp-inversion-80-never-is-fail
evals.prompt: We're about to sign off on a new self-managed MongoDB 8.0.4 Enterprise cluster on RHEL 9. Our platform team ran your check script on the primary and everything came back clean, see attached. They set transparent huge pages to never years ago as part of our standard MongoDB hardening image. Can you confirm we're good to go to production, or is anything actually wrong here?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the pasted run scored THP against pre-8.0 expectations. On 8.0 and later the documented value is enabled=always with defrag=defer+madvise, khugepaged/max_ptes_none=0 and vm.overcommit_memory=1, so enabled=never is a FAIL despite the [PASS] in the output. Gives a systemd-unit remediation and does not sign off. Phrases the finding as non-compliance with documented guidance rather than as a hard requirement.
expectations: States that MongoDB 8.0 and later document THP ENABLED, inverting the pre-8.0 guidance to disable it
Names the target value for transparent_hugepage/enabled as literally 'always' (not 'madvise' and not merely 'not never')
Classifies thp-enabled=never on this 8.0.4 host as FAIL, explicitly contradicting the [PASS] in the pasted output
Names the companion 8.0+ values: defrag=defer+madvise, khugepaged/max_ptes_none=0, vm.overcommit_memory=1
Flags max_ptes_none=511 and vm.overcommit_memory=0 as also wrong for 8.0, not merely informational

Provides a persistence remediation that survives reboot and names a concrete mechanism, such as a systemd unit ordered before mongod, a tuned profile, or the host build image. A runtime echo alone does not satisfy this.

States that this host is outside the kernel restriction AND gives the reason: kernel 5.14.0-427 is below 6.19, the lower bound of the affected range. A verdict with no version-based reason, or one reached by dismissing the check rather than by reasoning about the range, does not satisfy this.

evals.name: thp-inversion-70-never-is-pass
evals.prompt: Auditing a self-managed MongoDB 7.0.14 replica set on RHEL 9 before it goes live. Attached is the output from the host checks on one of the data-bearing nodes. Is the transparent huge pages configuration correct for this deployment, and is there anything blocking?
evals.expected_output: Confirms THP enabled=never and defrag=never are the documented values for 7.0 and a PASS. Does not apply the 8.0+ 'enable THP' guidance. Treats max_ptes_none and vm.overcommit_memory as not applicable on 7.0. Reports no blocking findings.
expectations: Confirms THP enabled=never is the documented value for MongoDB 7.0 and a PASS
Does NOT recommend enabling THP or setting defrag=defer+madvise on this 7.0 deployment
Treats khugepaged/max_ptes_none and vm.overcommit_memory as not applicable to 7.0 rather than as findings
States that kernel 5.14.0-427 is outside the kernel restriction and that 7.0 is unaffected regardless, rather than staying silent on the kernel
Names 8.0 as the point where THP guidance inverts, showing the verdict is version-aware rather than a restatement of the older disable-THP convention

evals.name: kernel-7014-not-a-remedy-on-8025
evals.prompt: Production is down. Rocky 9 box, MongoDB Enterprise 8.0.25, mongod won't stay up. We already hit the kernel 6.19 TCMalloc thing last quarter so the platform team upgraded this host to kernel 7.0.14, which the docs say resolves the incompatibility, but mongod still won't start. Attached is uname, the rpm version, systemctl and the tail of mongod.log. The platform team thinks the 7.0.14 upgrade didn't apply properly and wants to reimage the box tonight. What's actually happening and what do we do?
evals.expected_output: Explains that kernel 7.0.14 is not a remedy on MongoDB 8.0.25. Releases 8.0.21 through 8.0.29 and 8.3.0 through 8.3.8 exit during startup on any kernel 6.19 or later, including 7.0.14, because the startup guard was only narrowed in 8.0.30 and 8.3.9. The remedy is a MongoDB upgrade to 8.0.30 or later, not a kernel change or a reimage. Cites the log id 12257600 as the deliberate guard, not a failed upgrade.
expectations: States that kernel 7.0.14 does NOT resolve the problem on MongoDB 8.0.25
Explains that releases 8.0.21 through 8.0.29 exit during startup on any kernel 6.19 or later, 7.0.14 included
Identifies the remedy as upgrading MongoDB to 8.0.30 or later (or 8.3.9+/9.0), not changing the kernel

Tells the team NOT to reimage the host AND gives the correct reason: the host and kernel are fine, and the block comes from the MongoDB release. An answer that says not to reimage while attributing the failure to a bad kernel package, an invalid kernel version, or a failed kernel upgrade does not satisfy this.

Reads the mongod.log entry as a deliberate startup guard AND states what triggers it: this MongoDB release rejects kernel 6.19 and later by design. An answer that calls it a guard but attributes the trigger to an unsupported or non-existent kernel version does not satisfy this.
Does NOT advise downgrading the kernel back below 6.19 as the primary remedy

evals.name: wiredtiger-cache-both-set-and-selinux-js
evals.prompt: Inherited a self-managed MongoDB 8.3.4 box from a contractor and mongod is currently not running. Before I try to start it I want to know what's wrong with this config. Attached is mongod.conf plus free -g, the cgroup memory limit, getenforce and the version. The host has 62GB of RAM. Is the 48GB cache sane for this box, and is there anything else that will bite me?
evals.expected_output: Flags that cacheSizeGB and cacheSizePct are both set, which is a FAIL: exactly one of the two is permitted. Does not flag cacheSizePct 0.85 as above the 80 percent ceiling: the value is a percentage, so 0.85 means 0.85 percent. Flags that cacheSizeGB 48 is above the default of about 30.5 GB on a 62 GB host, which the documentation advises against. Flags that the 48GB cache exceeds the 32GB cgroup memory limit, so the container limit governs, not host RAM. Flags security.javascriptEnabled true under SELinux Enforcing as a FAIL that segfaults mongod. Notes bind_ip 0.0.0.0. Keeps config findings valid even though mongod is stopped, and marks runtime values UNKNOWN.
expectations: Flags that cacheSizeGB and cacheSizePct are both set as a FAIL, stating only one of the two may be configured
Does not report cacheSizePct 0.85 as above the 80 percent ceiling, reading the value as a percentage (0.85 percent) rather than a fraction
Flags security.javascriptEnabled true under SELinux Enforcing as a FAIL that causes mongod to segfault
Marks values that cannot be established from the pasted evidence as UNKNOWN with a reason, rather than PASS, while keeping the config-file findings valid despite mongod being stopped

evals.name: 90-inherits-80-expectations
evals.prompt: First MongoDB 9.0 deployment for us, 9.0.1 Enterprise on Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0.0-38-generic. Check output attached. Two questions from my team: our runbook says disable transparent huge pages for MongoDB, so are these three THP failures real or is the script scoring against the wrong version? And are we exposed to the kernel 6.19 issue on this kernel?
evals.expected_output: Confirms the THP failures are real: 9.0 inherits the 8.0-and-later expectations, so enabled=always and defrag=defer+madvise are documented and never is a FAIL. The runbook predates 8.0 and should be updated. On the kernel question, /proc/version_signature shows the 7.0.0-38-generic kernel is upstream 7.0.14, and 9.0 carries the narrowed, Ubuntu-aware guard, so the kernel is outside the restriction and this host is not exposed. May note that the Ubuntu 7.0.0-NNN label would still trip the guard on 8.0.30 to 8.0.34 and 8.3.9 to 8.3.13.
expectations: Confirms the three THP FAILs are real and that 9.0 follows the 8.0-and-later expectations (enabled=always, defrag=defer+madvise, max_ptes_none=0)
Tells the team their disable-THP runbook is outdated for 8.0 and later rather than validating it

States this host is NOT exposed to the kernel restriction, because 9.0 carries the narrowed guard and the 7.0.0-38-generic kernel is upstream 7.0.14 per /proc/version_signature, outside the affected range
Also flags vm.overcommit_memory=0 and the missing THP persistence mechanism as items to fix alongside

evals.name: container-node-scoping-unknown
evals._note: Coverage case, restored from iteration 1. Both configurations scored 5/5 there, so it is not expected to discriminate. It is retained because it is the only test of the documented container and Kubernetes edge case; a non-discriminating assertion is a reason to discount it in the delta, not a reason to stop testing the behaviour.
evals.prompt: I ran the production check inside our MongoDB container on Kubernetes rather than on the worker node, because that's the only shell I have. Output attached. Our SRE lead wants to close out the eight warnings as remediation tickets this sprint. Before I file them, is that the right read of this output?
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on treating the unreadable reads as actionable tickets. The /sys and /proc values that returned 'not found' or 'unreadable' belong to UNKNOWN with the reason carried, not WARN. Explains that THP, swappiness and zone_reclaim_mode are node-level settings not settable from inside the container, so they must be re-checked on the worker node. Separates the genuinely actionable finding, bind_ip 0.0.0.0, from the unverifiable ones.
expectations: Reclassifies the 'not found' and 'unreadable' /sys and /proc checks as UNKNOWN rather than WARN, because the run could not establish them
States that THP, vm.swappiness and vm.zone_reclaim_mode describe the worker node, not the pod, and must be verified on the node
Distinguishes which settings are settable from inside the container versus only on the node
Identifies bind_ip 0.0.0.0 as a genuinely actionable finding separate from the unverifiable ones
Advises against filing all eight warnings as remediation tickets as-is

evals.name: broad-coverage-all-categories
evals._note: Coverage case. Fixture is real, unedited output from a live Ubuntu 24.04 host (kernel 6.17, unprivileged run, mongod not installed), redacted only for hostname and NIC names. Exercises the categories no other eval touches: storage, network, NUMA, clock, ulimits, TCMalloc and security.
evals.prompt: Pre-install audit for a new self-managed MongoDB 8.0.25 Enterprise deployment on an Azure VM running Ubuntu 24.04. mongod is not installed yet. I ran the full check suite as my normal login, not as root. Full output attached. Give me the prioritised remediation list I should hand to the platform team, and tell me what this run could not establish.
evals.expected_output: Produces a prioritised list led by the two FAILs (vm.swappiness 60 and ulimit-processes 31436) and covering the WARN items across every category: ulimits (nofile 1024, nproc 31436, no limits.d file), network (tcp_keepalive_time 7200, syn_backlog 512, netdev_max_backlog 1000), kernel (dirty_ratio 20, dirty_background_ratio 10), THP (defrag madvise, max_ptes_none 511, overcommit_memory 0, no persistence), and storage (dbPath absent). States that mongod not being installed is expected for a pre-install audit and that the process, WiredTiger runtime and config findings are consequently unestablished. Confirms kernel 6.17 is below 6.19 so the deployment is clear of the kernel restriction, and that Ubuntu 24.04 is supported on 8.0.
expectations: Leads with the two FAIL items, vm.swappiness 60 and ulimit-processes 31436, as the blocking pre-install work, ahead of the WARN items
Covers ulimits: processes 31436 is a blocking FAIL below the 32768 threshold, open files soft 1024 is below the 64000 recommendation, and no mongod limits file exists in /etc/security/limits.d/
Covers network tuning: tcp_keepalive_time 7200 against the recommended 120, plus at least one of tcp_max_syn_backlog 512 or netdev_max_backlog 1000

Covers kernel tuning: vm.dirty_ratio 20 (recommended 10 to 15) and vm.dirty_background_ratio 10 (recommended 3 to 5) are WARN, described as informational guidance with no MongoDB public reference, not as blocking
Covers THP for 8.0: defrag=madvise, khugepaged/max_ptes_none=511 and vm.overcommit_memory=0 are all wrong for this version, and no persistence mechanism is configured
Covers storage: dbPath /var/lib/mongo does not exist, which is expected before install but must be created and owned by the mongod user
Reports the clock checks as satisfied rather than omitting them, since a time daemon is running and synchronised
Reports NUMA as not applicable on this host because it presents a single NUMA node, rather than recommending numactl interleaving anyway
States that kernel 6.17 is below 6.19 and therefore outside the documented kernel restriction for 8.0.25
Treats mongod not being installed as expected for a pre-install audit rather than as a failure, and does not report the absent mongod.conf as a blocking finding
Identifies what the run could not establish, including the runtime and WiredTiger values that need a live server, rather than reporting them as passing

evals.name: amazonlinux-thp-madvise-selinux-permissive
evals._note: Second broad-coverage case, on a different distro from eval 7. Fixture is real, redacted output from an Amazon Linux 2023 EC2 host: kernel 6.18.48 (one minor version below the 6.19 boundary), THP at madvise, SELinux Permissive, ulimits already correct, and 0.8 GB RAM so the WiredTiger 0.256 GB cache floor applies. Covers the middle THP state and the SELinux path that eval 7's Ubuntu host cannot reach.
evals.prompt: Sizing exercise before we commit to an instance type. This is an Amazon Linux 2023 EC2 box we're considering for a self-managed MongoDB 8.0.25 node, nothing installed yet. Full check output attached. Our platform standard sets transparent huge pages to madvise across the fleet and we run SELinux in Permissive because Enforcing broke an unrelated agent last year. Two questions: are those two fleet standards a problem for MongoDB here, and is this instance actually big enough?
evals.expected_output: Says THP=madvise is a WARN rather than a PASS on 8.0.25, since 8.0 and later document enabled=always, and madvise is the middle state that is suboptimal on every version. Says SELinux Permissive is a WARN and not blocking, and notes the skill's related concern is that server-side JavaScript under Enforcing segfaults mongod, so moving to Enforcing needs javascriptEnabled checked first. On sizing, flags 0.8 GB RAM and 2 cores as the real problem: the WiredTiger cache falls back to the 0.256 GB floor because 50 percent of (RAM - 1GB) is negative, which is unusable for production. Confirms kernel 6.18.48 is below 6.19 and outside the restriction. Notes ulimits already pass on this host.
expectations: States THP=madvise is a WARN on MongoDB 8.0.25, not a PASS, because 8.0 and later document enabled=always
Explains that madvise is the middle state and is suboptimal on every MongoDB version, rather than treating it as correct for one of them
Identifies SELinux Permissive as a non-blocking WARN rather than a FAIL
Raises that server-side JavaScript under SELinux Enforcing segfaults mongod, so javascriptEnabled must be checked before moving this host to Enforcing
Flags 0.8 GB total RAM as the dominant sizing problem, not the THP or SELinux settings
States that the WiredTiger cache falls back to the 0.256 GB floor on this host because 50 percent of (RAM minus 1GB) is at or below the floor
States that kernel 6.18.48 is below 6.19 and therefore outside the documented kernel restriction
Notes that the open files limit already meets the recommendation on this host at 65535, rather than repeating generic nofile advice
Notes that the processes limit is already unlimited on this host, rather than repeating generic nproc advice
Recommends a larger instance before production rather than declaring the host ready once THP and SELinux are addressed

evals.name: 60-out-of-scope-rescored-as-70
evals._note: Tests the prerequisite stop rule for an unsupported version. The fixture shows the suite rejecting --version 6.0, then a re-run forced to --version 7.0 on a 6.0.19 binary. Everything except the version lines passes, which invites a 'sign off the rest' answer.
evals.prompt: Pre go-live check on a self-managed MongoDB Enterprise replica set on RHEL 8.10. The nodes run 6.0.19. Your script refused --version 6.0, so we re-ran it with --version 7.0 since that is the closest one it accepts. Output from the primary attached. Apart from the version lines everything is green, and we already have the upgrade booked for Q1. Can you sign off the rest of this audit as production-ready so we can go live next week and deal with the version later?
evals.expected_output: Declines to sign off. MongoDB 6.0 is outside the versions this audit has expected values for (7.0, 8.0, 8.3, 9.0), so forcing --version 7.0 scores a 6.0.19 binary against the wrong expectations and the green results are not evidence of readiness for this deployment. States that 6.0 is end of life (July 31, 2025) and that going live on it means running an unsupported release. Recommends upgrading before go-live rather than in Q1, notes that a 6.0 deployment upgrades one major release at a time with 7.0 as the next step, and points to the MongoDB lifecycle schedule or the MongoDB account team. Offers to run the full audit once the nodes are on a covered release, with --version matching the installed binary.
expectations: Refuses to certify the host or the remaining checks as production-ready
Explains that the --version 7.0 re-run grades a 6.0.19 binary against another release's expected values, so its PASS results cannot stand in for an audit of this deployment
States that MongoDB 6.0 is past end of life, with July 31, 2025 as the date, and that going live on it means running an unsupported release
Advises completing the upgrade before go-live instead of deferring it to Q1
Describes the upgrade path as one major release at a time, moving to 7.0 first rather than jumping straight to 8.0 or later
Directs the team to the MongoDB lifecycle schedule or to their MongoDB account team for support status
Does not present a per-check PASS/WARN/FAIL scorecard for this host as the audit result
Offers to audit again after the upgrade, with the --version argument matching the installed mongod

evals.name: 70-host-built-from-80-golden-image
evals._note: Inverse of eval 1 and complement to eval 2. A 7.0.21 node built from a golden image tuned for 8.0, audited with --version 8.0. The run is green apart from the version-mismatch WARN, but THP always and defrag defer+madvise are FAILs on 7.0, and the tuned profile reasserts them every boot.
evals.prompt: Our platform team builds every MongoDB host from one golden RHEL 9.4 image that follows the 8.0 production notes, including the THP settings. This new node joins a self-managed MongoDB 7.0.21 Enterprise replica set that will stay on 7.0 until next year. They ran the suite with --version 8.0 because that is what the image is certified against, and the only thing flagged is a version-mismatch warning they want to ignore. Output attached. Is this node ready to join the 7.0 replica set?
evals.expected_output: Says the node is not ready. The run scored a 7.0.21 binary against 8.0 expectations, so the mismatch warning invalidates the green result rather than being ignorable. Re-scored for 7.0, THP enabled=always is a FAIL and defrag=defer+madvise is a FAIL, because 7.0 documents never for both. max_ptes_none=0 and vm.overcommit_memory=1 are not 7.0 checks, so they are not reported as passes that matter here. The tuned profile golden-mongodb-80 reasserts the wrong values on every boot, so the fix is a 7.0-specific tuned profile or image variant rather than a runtime echo. The TCMalloc and kernel 6.19 checks are 8.0-only; kernel 5.14 is fine and 7.0 is unaffected by the restriction anyway. Recommends re-running with --version 7.0 after the change.
expectations: States the node is not ready to join the 7.0 replica set as configured
Treats the mongod-version-match warning as invalidating the whole run, not as a cosmetic warning to ignore
Classifies THP enabled=always on this 7.0.21 host as FAIL, contradicting the [PASS] in the output
Classifies defrag=defer+madvise as wrong for 7.0, where the documented value is never
Does not count khugepaged/max_ptes_none or vm.overcommit_memory as 7.0 passes, treating them as checks that apply from 8.0 on

Identifies the active tuned profile golden-mongodb-80 as the reason the wrong THP values come back after every reboot, and proposes a 7.0-specific tuned profile, image variant or systemd unit as the persistent fix
Notes the TCMalloc section and its kernel check are 8.0-only, and that 7.0 is not affected by the kernel 6.19 restriction
Recommends re-running the suite with --version 7.0 after the THP change before the node joins

evals.name: 80-ppc64le-thp-always
evals._note: THP on ppc64le and s390x. The TCMalloc page says MongoDB uses the legacy TCMalloc on these architectures regardless of OS version and to disable THP. The fixture shows output from an older checker that scored always as correct for every 8.0 host.
evals.prompt: Our MongoDB 8.0.4 Enterprise host is RHEL 9 on ppc64le. We followed the 8.0 production notes and set THP to always, defer+madvise, max_ptes_none 0 and overcommit 1, and the THP check passes. Output attached. Is the THP configuration correct for this host?
evals.expected_output: Says the configuration is not correct for this host. On ppc64le MongoDB uses the legacy TCMalloc at every version, regardless of OS version, and the TCMalloc page says to disable THP on PPC64LE and s390x. THP enabled=always is a FAIL and defrag should be never. The 8.0 values (always, defer+madvise, max_ptes_none 0, overcommit 1) belong to the updated TCMalloc on x86_64 and arm64. The PASS lines in the attached output come from the x86_64 rule and do not apply here. Recommends setting THP to never and persisting it, then re-running the check.
expectations: States the THP configuration is not correct for a ppc64le host even though the supplied output shows PASS
Explains that ppc64le and s390x use the legacy TCMalloc regardless of operating system version and that the documentation says to disable THP on them
Identifies enabled=always as a FAIL on this architecture and recommends never
Does not apply the x86_64 and arm64 8.0 rule (always, defer+madvise, max_ptes_none 0, overcommit 1) to this host
Presents the fix as a change for the user to approve and run, not as applied by the audit

evals.name: 8034-ubuntu-kernel-labelled-700
evals._note: Ubuntu labels a kernel carrying the rseq fix as 7.0.0-NNN. On 8.0.30 to 8.0.34 and 8.3.9 to 8.3.13 the literal version guard still trips; the fix is in 8.0.35 and 8.3.14 (SERVER-131779). No release date may be stated.
evals.prompt: Ubuntu 24.04 GCP VM, MongoDB Enterprise 8.0.34, mongod will not stay up. The kernel is the Ubuntu 7.0.0 build and /proc/version_signature says 7.0.14, so it should be past the 6.19 to 7.0.13 problem. Attached is the evidence. What is going on and what do we do?
evals.expected_output: Explains that Ubuntu labels the kernel 7.0.0-1011-gcp even though /proc/version_signature shows it carries the 7.0.14 fix, and that mongod 8.0.34 compares the kernel version literally, so it exits during startup. The Ubuntu-aware guard is in MongoDB 8.0.35 and 8.3.14 (SERVER-131779). The remedy is a MongoDB upgrade to 8.0.35 or later; upgrading the Ubuntu kernel package does not help while it keeps the 7.0.0 label, though a kernel labelled 7.0.14 or later would also clear the guard. States no release date for 8.0.35 or 8.3.14. Presents the fix as a command for the user to run after approval.
expectations: Identifies the 7.0.0-1011-gcp label as the cause even though /proc/version_signature reports 7.0.14
Identifies the remedy as upgrading MongoDB to 8.0.35 or later (or 8.3.14 or later), not changing the kernel
Does not state or imply a release date or availability for 8.0.35 or 8.3.14
Does not present reimaging or an Ubuntu kernel package upgrade as the fix, since the 7.0.0 label stays; may note that a kernel labelled 7.0.14 or later would also clear the guard
Does not quote internal Slack or ticket discussion; cites SERVER-125742 and SERVER-131779 only

evals.name: 8025-kernel-6192-roll-forward-not-a-fix
evals._note: Reviewer case (PR #70): on 8.0.21-8.0.29 a kernel in 6.19-7.0.13 must not be answered with 'move to kernel 7.0.14'. Both columns are ge_619. Raw command output, like eval 3.
evals.prompt: Rocky 9 on Graviton, MongoDB Enterprise 8.0.25. The kernel team pushed 6.19.2 to this replica set member last night and mongod won't start. The production notes say kernels 6.19 through 7.0.13 are affected and 7.0.14 resolves it, so the plan is to roll the host forward to 7.0.14 in tonight's window. Evidence attached. Is that the right fix?
evals.expected_output: Says rolling forward to kernel 7.0.14 will not fix it: 8.0.21 through 8.0.29 exit during startup on any kernel 6.19 or later, 7.0.14 included, so the documented 7.0.14 resolution does not apply to this release. Reads the 12257600 and 12257601 log entries as mongod's deliberate startup guard for this release, not a broken kernel. Gives the working remedies: boot the previous 5.14 kernel, which grubby shows is still installed (below 6.19); or upgrade MongoDB to 8.0.30 or later (or 8.3.9 or later, or 9.0) and run it on kernel 7.0.14 or later, since 8.0.30 on 6.19.2 still exits. Does not describe this as the 8.0.0 to 8.0.20 data-corruption band: 8.0.25 refuses to start. Presents the change for approval and a one-member-at-a-time window.
expectations: States that rolling forward to kernel 7.0.14 does NOT fix mongod 8.0.25
Explains that 8.0.21 through 8.0.29 exit during startup on any kernel 6.19 or later, 7.0.14 included
Offers booting a kernel below 6.19 (for example the installed 5.14 kernel) as a working remedy

When it recommends a MongoDB upgrade, pairs it with kernel 7.0.14 or later or a kernel below 6.19, because 8.0.30 and later still exit on 6.19.2. An answer that says a MongoDB upgrade alone fixes this host on 6.19.2 does not satisfy this.
Reads the log entries as mongod's deliberate startup guard for this MongoDB release, not as a defective or failed kernel
Does not describe the failure as the 8.0.0-8.0.20 crash or data-corruption risk; 8.0.25 refuses to start

evals.name: selinux-js-omitted-nested-tls-old-script
evals._note: Reviewer cases (PR #70): javascriptEnabled omitted under Enforcing defaults to true; nested net.tls.mode was missed by the old line-matching check. The attached check-security.sh output is real output of the pre-fix scripts.
evals.prompt: Security asked me to close out two items from our October audit of a MongoDB Enterprise 8.0.30 replica set member on Rocky 9 with SELinux Enforcing. The audit flagged TLS as not configured, which I think is wrong because we require TLS, and it passed the SELinux JavaScript check, so we planned to leave that alone. The current config, getenforce, the version and the October output are attached. Can I close the TLS item, and is there anything to do on JavaScript?
evals.expected_output: Confirms the TLS warning is a false positive: net.tls.mode is requireTLS in the nested net: tls: block, so TLS is required and the item can be closed; the October check matched lines rather than the scoped key. Overturns the JavaScript PASS: security.javascriptEnabled is not set, it defaults to true, and under SELinux any operation that needs server-side JavaScript segfaults mongod. Recommends setting security.javascriptEnabled: false, or starting mongod with --noscripting, after confirming the application does not use server-side JavaScript, applied one member at a time. Recommends re-running the current scripts rather than relying on the October output. The encryption-at-rest WARN is a recommendation for regulated environments, not a blocker.
expectations: Confirms the TLS finding is a false positive because net.tls.mode is requireTLS in the nested net.tls block, and says the TLS item can be closed
Overturns the selinux-javascript PASS, stating that javascriptEnabled is not set and defaults to true
States that under SELinux Enforcing, operations that need server-side JavaScript segfault mongod
Recommends security.javascriptEnabled: false (or --noscripting), conditioned on confirming the application does not rely on server-side JavaScript
Does not treat the October output as settled evidence for either item, and recommends re-checking with the current scripts
Does not tell the user to configure TLS or change the net.tls settings

evals.name: 70-ubuntu2404-root-run-dbpath
evals._note: Reviewer cases (PR #70): dbPath access is tested as the service user, not the auditing user; OS support is version-specific (7.0 is not listed for Ubuntu 24.04). Real output of the fixed scripts, filtered by the grep shown in each command.
evals.prompt: We moved a MongoDB Enterprise 7.0.21 replica set member onto a new Ubuntu 24.04 Graviton host (24.04 is LTS, so it should be fine) and restored the data from backup into /var/lib/mongodb. mongod fails with permission denied on the data directory. I ran your checks with sudo and they say dbpath-permissions FAIL, but as root I can write to that directory fine, so the script looks wrong to me. Output attached. What's actually wrong?
evals.expected_output: The script is right: it tests access as the MongoDB service user, mongodb on Ubuntu, not as root, and root bypasses the permission check. The restore left /var/lib/mongodb owned root:root with mode 750, so mongodb cannot traverse it. Fix: chown -R mongodb:mongodb /var/lib/mongodb and confirm the parent directories are traversable, then start mongod. Separately, MongoDB Enterprise 7.0 is not supported on Ubuntu 24.04: the support matrix lists 24.04 for 8.x and 9.x only, LTS or not. Supported paths are 7.0 on Ubuntu 22.04, or upgrading to 8.0 on 24.04. Kernel 6.8 carries no kernel finding for 7.0. Changes are presented for approval.
expectations: Explains that the dbpath check is correct because it tests access as the mongodb service user, and that root can write to the directory regardless of its ownership or mode
Identifies the root:root ownership with mode 750 left by the restore as the cause of the permission-denied startup failure
Gives the fix as chown -R mongodb:mongodb /var/lib/mongodb, using the mongodb account rather than mongod
States that MongoDB 7.0 is not supported on Ubuntu 24.04, even though 24.04 is an LTS release
Offers a supported path: 7.0 on Ubuntu 22.04, or upgrading to MongoDB 8.0 on Ubuntu 24.04
Does not raise a kernel 6.19 finding for this host, since 7.0 is unaffected and kernel 6.8 is below 6.19

evals.name: 8025-run-as-8030-unprivileged-incomplete
evals._note: Reviewer cases (PR #70): the version-match check compares the patch; failed reads are UNKNOWN; a category that exits non-zero is recorded as UNKNOWN. Real output of the fixed scripts from an unprivileged run.
evals.prompt: Maintenance window on a Rocky 9 Graviton host: the platform team patched it to kernel 7.0.14 and rebooted, and mongod is still stopped. Before we start it I ran the audit as my own login with --version 8.0.30, since that's what our build standard says we run. Kernel and TCMalloc both pass. Can we start mongod and close the window? Output attached.
evals.expected_output: Do not start mongod or close the window yet. The run was scored as 8.0.30, but the installed binary is 8.0.25 (mongod-version-match WARN), so the kernel and TCMalloc PASS lines do not apply. On 8.0.25, mongod exits during startup on any kernel 6.19 or later, 7.0.14 included, so starting it will fail. Remedy: upgrade MongoDB to 8.0.30 or later, which the build standard already calls for, before starting it; or boot a kernel below 6.19. Re-run the audit with the installed version. The run is incomplete: the Network category did not run (check-network.sh is missing, exit status 127), so recopy the scripts. The config could not be read, so authorization, TLS, the WiredTiger cache and JavaScript under SELinux Enforcing are UNKNOWN; javascriptEnabled defaults to true, which matters under Enforcing. dbPath access is UNKNOWN for the mongod user. Re-run with sudo. Real findings to fix: vm.swappiness 60 and no time daemon (FAIL), THP defrag and max_ptes_none (WARN), and the missing limits file.
expectations: Says not to start mongod, or not to close the window, on this evidence
Identifies that the run was scored against 8.0.30 while 8.0.25 is installed, so the kernel and TCMalloc PASS lines do not apply
States that MongoDB 8.0.25 exits during startup on kernel 7.0.14 (any kernel 6.19 or later), so starting mongod as installed will fail
Gives the remedy as upgrading MongoDB to 8.0.30 or later before starting, or booting a kernel below 6.19, not a further kernel upgrade
Treats the Network category as not run (check-network.sh missing, exit status 127) rather than as passed, and asks for the scripts to be recopied and re-run
Treats the config-dependent checks (authorization, TLS, WiredTiger cache, JavaScript under SELinux) as UNKNOWN because the config could not be read, not as passed, and asks for a re-run with sudo
Reports the vm.swappiness 60 and missing time daemon FAILs
Asks for the re-run to use the installed MongoDB version (8.0.25, or the new version after an upgrade) rather than 8.0.30
